extraShopItems.name: Hand-Dyed Tenugui Cotton Cloth
extraShopItems.story: Versatile Japanese flat-woven cotton hand towels dyed using the traditional chusen stencil technique with Mt. Fuji and cherry blossom motifs.
extraShopItems.whereToBuy: Kamawanu in Daikanyama or Asakusa artisan stalls.
extraShopItems.tip: Edges are left unhemmed intentionally to dry rapidly and prevent bacteria growth.

extraShopItems.name: Edo Kiriko Cut Glass Tumbler
extraShopItems.story: Tokyo's designated traditional craft: clear crystal layered with vivid cobalt or crimson glass and precision geometric cut patterns.
extraShopItems.whereToBuy: Edo Kiriko Cooperative Showroom in Kameido or Nihombashi Mitsukoshi.
extraShopItems.tip: Traditional 'nanako' fish-scale cuts catch and refract light like diamonds.

extraShopItems.name: Echizen Washi Paper Letter Set
extraShopItems.story: Handmade 1,500-year heritage washi crafted with kozo (mulberry) fibers with natural deckled edges and botanical pressings.
extraShopItems.whereToBuy: Haibara in Nihombashi (established 1806) or Itoya Ginza.
extraShopItems.tip: Smooth surface is optimized for fountain pens without ink bleed-through.

extraShopItems.name: Studio Ghibli & Anime Figures
extraShopItems.story: Authentic licensed figures, music boxes, and plushies from My Neighbor Totoro, Spirited Away, and modern anime series.
extraShopItems.whereToBuy: Donguri Kyowakoku Tokyo Station or Mandarake Nakano Broadway.
extraShopItems.tip: Bring your passport to Donguri Kyowakoku for immediate 10% tax-free refund.

extraShopItems.name: Kyoto Incense & Ceramic Burner
extraShopItems.story: Pure sandalwood and agarwood incense sticks handcrafted using centuries-old temple recipes, with a ceramic incense dish.
extraShopItems.whereToBuy: Shoyeido Incense Ginza branch or Kyoto main store.
extraShopItems.tip: Look for 'Horie' floral blends for modern living spaces.

extraShopItems.name: Traditional Yukata & Geta Set
extraShopItems.story: Lightweight unlined cotton summer kimono with matching woven obi sash and wooden geta clogs.
extraShopItems.whereToBuy: Kimono Yamato or Oriental Bazaar in Omotesando.
extraShopItems.tip: Pre-tied obi sash options are available for effortless self-dressing.

items: Ichiran Shibuya & Fuunji Shinjuku
Tokyo. Legendary solo-booth tonkotsu ramen and rich dipping tsukemen noodles.
Tsukiji Outer Market
Tokyo. Fresh morning sashimi bowls, grilled scallops, tamagoyaki skewers, and wagyu beef.
Omoide Yokocho & Golden Gai
Shinjuku. Atmospheric narrow lantern-lit alleyways packed with sizzling charcoal yakitori stands.
Suzukien Asakusa
Asakusa. Historic tea house famed for the world’s most intense Level 7 ceremonial matcha gelato.
Tap water
Clean, refreshing, and served free in ice glasses at every restaurant.
Tipping
Not customary in Japan. Good service is standard and tips may be politely declined.
Slurping
Slurping ramen and soba noodles cools them down and is considered a compliment to the chef.
Cash stalls
Many traditional ticket vending ramen shops and street stalls only accept ¥1,000 bills and coins.
Convenience
7-Eleven, Lawson, and FamilyMart offer exceptional freshly-prepared onigiri, egg sandos, and hot fried chicken.
Kappabashi Kitchen Town
Taito. 170+ shops specializing in hand-forged Japanese knives, ceramics, lacquerware, and cookware.
Ginza Itoya
Ginza. 12-story stationery wonderland with custom paper, fountain pens, traveler notebooks, and washi tapes.
Nakamise-dori Asakusa
Asakusa. Ancient market street selling sensu folding fans, yukata, wooden kokeshi dolls, and senbei crackers.
Haneda & Narita Duty-Free
Airport. Buy regional KitKats, Royce chocolate, and tax-free ceramics right before boarding.
Tax refund
Foreign tourists can claim 10% consumption tax refund on purchases over ¥5,000. Carry your physical passport.
Payment
Suica / Pasmo transit IC cards and credit cards are widely accepted at convenience stores and department stores.
Authentic marks
Look for 'Made in Japan' and prefecture marks like 'Mino-yaki' or 'Kyo-Sensu' to avoid cheap factory imports.
Store hours
Most department stores open at 10:00 or 11:00 AM and close around 8:00 PM.
Luggage packing
Knives must be packed inside checked baggage. Ask shops for protective bubble wrap for ceramics and glass.
